title: Does bundling make it safe?
text: You guess bundling your server as an MCPB is what makes it safe to run. It isn't. Bundling only means it runs without your dev tool chain installed. Safety is still entirely on you. Here, package my server as an MCPB, and it's easy to assume the bundle itself has been made safer, like putting the code in a container.

title: Same access as the raw script
text: But open the manifest, and there's no permissions block, no sandbox field, nothing to check. A packaged MCPB runs with exactly the same file access as the original unpackaged script. Package a path bug into it, and it walks outside its own folder exactly as easily. Here's

title: The anchor — one env variable
text: The anchor. Say your manifest launches the server with one setting, an environment variable named root d i r pointing at the folder the user picked at install time. An MCPB is a zip, manifest, JSON, a server folder with your code and dependencies, and an icon. The host reads the manifest and launches MCP config's command exactly as written. Dollar dir name for bundle relative paths, dollar user config for install time values like that folder the user picked. The env var name is exactly what

title: Wrong name, no error
text: You wrote in the manifest. No auto prefix, no transform. Write root d i r in the manifest, but read root directory in your server code, and the value comes back silently empty. No error, no crash. The config is just quietly ignored. So back to root dir, get the name right, and that path flows straight into your handler with no check on it at all. Because there's no sandbox, one unvalidated {slash} in a file name walks the server right out of its own folder.

title: Neither result is proof
text: A packaged MCPB that runs fine on your machine doesn't prove it's safe anywhere else. It may only prove your own dev tool chain quietly filled a gap. And an MCPB that fails on a clean machine doesn't mean the packaging step is broken. It usually means one dependency never actually got bundled in.

title: The carry-out
text: Packaging a server as an MCPB makes it runnable without a tool chain. It doesn't make it safe. The env var name still has to match exactly, and every path check is still yours to write. Your turn. Paste this

title: Your turn
text: Into Claude. Build an MCPB that reads files from a directory the user configures at install time. Watch three things. Does the env var name in the manifest MCP config exactly match what the server code reads? Does the server validate that every requested path stays inside that configured root or would a dot dot slash escape it? And does the build script bundle dependencies with esbuild or does it assume node modules will already be there? Build MCPB Liam in for Bear.
